about: What the native parity views expect from the web app's published data.
The key sets and types are NOT in this file. Those are read out of the Swift
source by .github/scripts/parity-schema.mjs, so they cannot go stale against
the code. This file carries only the three things the Swift cannot tell a
endpoints      which URL feeds which document type. Derivable for the
views that hold a `static let dataURL`, but several build
their URL from a root and a relative path, so the mapping
is written out once here for all of them.
closedSets     string fields the Swift switches over. These never throw —
each switch has a `default` — so a new value degrades
silently instead of failing loudly. That is why they need
markupMirrors  prose and tables copied out of a web page's markup because
they are in no published JSON file. They will not follow an
edit on the web side, so the check watches the page.
Every value below was read off the live site, not guessed.

endpoints.note: The view asks for authorized-<year>.json for whichever year is selected. One year stands in for the family; they are generated by the same script.

closedSets.consequence: An unhandled status takes the default branch: a grey dot with no colour and no glyph, on a page whose whole argument is which years were lawful.
An unhandled code is shown raw and tinted grey, so a reader sees "W" instead of a party name. Matches the web page's own fallback, but the web page would have been updated.
An unhandled status sorts to the bottom of the roster rather than into its intended group. Its wording still comes from the document's statusLabels, so the label itself survives.
loadShard returns an empty array for a missing key, so a whole search category disappears from results without any error.

phrases: Private-sector business owners have no public pension at all
markupMirrors.note: The distinction the page rests on — drawing a pension versus building one. In the markup, not in officials-pensions.json.

The five steps OSC applies, in order. Describes statute rather than Riverhead's numbers, so it does not go stale the way a figure would — but a reworded step on the web side would leave the two out of step.
Only the labels for party codes currently in the data are rendered on the page, so this checks the two that are. The full code set is covered by the candidate-party closed set.

unchecked.reason: Reached through shard files whose names the manifest supplies at runtime. The manifest itself is checked, and search-shards covers the failure that actually bites — a category going missing.
BudgetLiveParityView holds the route table; it decodes no document of its own.
